result.topic_en: Using a rectangular table of residues to count the numbers coprime to a, Euler derives π(a^m)=a^{m-1}π(a) and the multiplicativity π(ab)=π(a)π(b) for coprime a, b (π being Euler's totient function), and gives a small table of values.
result.transcription:
Fragmentorum ex Adversariis continuatio. 493
$$\begin{array}{ccccc|c} 1 & \alpha & \beta & \gamma \;\ldots\; a-1 & & a \\ a+1 & a+\alpha & a+\beta & a+\gamma \;\ldots\; a-1 & & 2a \\ 2a+1 & 2a+\alpha & 2a+\beta & 2a+\gamma \;\ldots\; 3a-1 & & 3a \\ 3a+1 & 3a+\alpha & 3a+\beta & 3a+\gamma \;\ldots\; 4a-1 & & 4a \\ \ldots & \ldots & \ldots & \ldots & & \ldots \\ (n-1)a+1, & (n-1)a+\alpha, & (n-1)a+\beta, & (n-1)a+\gamma \ldots\; na-1 & & na \end{array}$$
Quemadmodum igitur hic prima series horizontalis continet omnes numeros ad $a$ primos ab 0 usque ad $a$, ita secunda series continet omnes ad $a$ primos usque ad $2a$, tertia vero omnes numeros ad $a$ primos ab $2a$ usque ad $3a$, hocque modo hae series continuentur usque ad ultimam $(n-1)a+1$. Omnes igitur, conjunctim praebent omnes numeros ad $a$ primos ab 0 usque ad $na$, quorum ergo numerus est $n\pi a$. Singulae autem series verticales erunt arithmeticae progressiones differentia $a$ crescentes. His praemissis sequentia problemata facillime solventur.
Problema. Proposito numero quocunque $a$, investigare valores formularum $\pi a^2$, $\pi a^3$, $\pi a^4$, et in genere $\pi a^m$.
Solutio. In schemate superiore sumamus $n=a$, ut quaeratur $\pi a^2$, atque manifestum est omnes terminos illarum serierum, quia sunt primi ad $a$, etiam primos fore ad $aa$. Quare cum earum serierum numerus sit $n=a$, et cujusque terminorum numerus $=\pi a$, omnino habebimus $a.\pi a$, cui ergo aequalis $\pi aa$, ita ut sit $\pi aa = a\pi a$. Deinde sumto $n=aa$, ut sit $na=a^3$, quia iterum omnes termini sunt primi ad $a^3$, eorum numerus erit $aa\pi a$, ideoque $\pi a^3 = aa\pi a$. Atque in genere si sumatur $n=a^{m-1}$, ut fiat $na=a^m$, multitudo omnium numerorum ad $a^m$ primorum erit
$$a^{m-1}\pi a.$$
Coroll. Si igitur $a$ numerus primus, ideoque $\pi a = a-1$, erit
$$\pi a^2 = a(a-1), \quad \pi a^3 = aa(a-1) \quad \text{et} \ldots \pi a^m = a^{m-1}(a-1).$$
Problema. Propositis duobus numeris $a$ et $b$ inter se primis, pro quibus habeantur formulae $\pi a$ et $\pi b$, invenire multitudinem omnium numerorum ad productum $ab$ primorum ipsoque minorum, sive investigare valorem $\pi ab$.
Solutio. In schemate superiore sumatur $n=b$, ut fiat $na=ab$; et quia series horizontales continent omnes numeros ad $a$ primos ab 1 usque ad $ab$, quorum ergo numerus est $b\pi a$, jam consideretur prima series verticalis, quae est $1, a+1, 2a+1, \ldots (b-1)a+1$, quae quia est arithmetica, ejusque differentia $a$ est prima ad $b$, numerus terminorum ad $b$ primorum $=\pi b$. Hoc idem valet de reliquis seriebus verticalibus, quarum quaelibet $\pi b$ continet terminos ad $b$ primos. Quamobrem numerus omnium terminorum simul ad $a$ et $b$ primorum, ob numerum verticalium $=\pi a$, erit $=\pi a.\pi b$, ita ut sit $\pi ab = \pi a.\pi b$.
Hinc jam tabula pro omnibus numeris condi poterit:
$$\begin{array}{llll} \pi 1 = 1 & \pi 5 = 4 & \pi 9 = 6 & \pi 13 = 12 \\ \pi 2 = 1 & \pi 6 = 2 & \pi 10 = 4 & \pi 14 = 6 \\ \pi 3 = 2 & \pi 7 = 6 & \pi 11 = 10 & \pi 15 = 8 \\ \pi 4 = 2 & \pi 8 = 4 & \pi 12 = 4 & \pi 16 = 7 \;\text{etc.} \end{array}$$
Hinc porro patet, si fuerint $a, b, c, d$ numeri inter se primi, tum fore $\pi abcd = \pi a.\pi b.\pi c.\pi d$. Hinc similiter, si proponatur numerus $a^\alpha b^\beta c^\gamma d^\delta = N$, erit $\pi N = a^{\alpha-1}\pi a.b^{\beta-1}\pi b.c^{\gamma-1}\pi c.d^{\delta-1}\pi d$.
A. m. T. III. p. 182 — 184.

items.quote: Proposito numero quocunque $a$, investigare valores formularum $\pi a^2$, $\pi a^3$, $\pi a^4$, et in genere $\pi a^m$.
items.english: Given any number a, to find the values of the expressions πa², πa³, πa⁴, and in general πa^m.

items.quote:
Si igitur $a$ numerus primus, ideoque $\pi a = a-1$, erit
$$\pi a^2 = a(a-1), \quad \pi a^3 = aa(a-1) \quad \text{et} \ldots \pi a^m = a^{m-1}(a-1).$$
items.english: If therefore a is a prime number, so that πa = a−1, then πa² = a(a−1), πa³ = a²(a−1), and in general πa^m = a^{m−1}(a−1).

items.quote: Propositis duobus numeris $a$ et $b$ inter se primis, pro quibus habeantur formulae $\pi a$ et $\pi b$, invenire multitudinem omnium numerorum ad productum $ab$ primorum ipsoque minorum, sive investigare valorem $\pi ab$.
items.english: Given two coprime numbers a and b, for which πa and πb are known, to find how many numbers are coprime to the product ab and smaller than it, that is, to find the value of πab.

items.quote: Hinc porro patet, si fuerint $a, b, c, d$ numeri inter se primi, tum fore $\pi abcd = \pi a.\pi b.\pi c.\pi d$.
items.english: Hence it is further clear that if a, b, c, d are pairwise coprime numbers, then πabcd = πa·πb·πc·πd.

items.quote: Hinc similiter, si proponatur numerus $a^\alpha b^\beta c^\gamma d^\delta = N$, erit $\pi N = a^{\alpha-1}\pi a.b^{\beta-1}\pi b.c^{\gamma-1}\pi c.d^{\delta-1}\pi d$.
items.english: Similarly, if the number N = a^α b^β c^γ d^δ is given, then πN = a^{α−1}πa · b^{β−1}πb · c^{γ−1}πc · d^{δ−1}πd.
